itemOffered.name: Youth Crimes Defence
itemOffered.description: Youth crime is a criminal allegation against someone under 18. Most cases are heard in the Youth Court, which has its own procedure and considers the young person's welfare. Astons Law Chambers acts for clients under 18 in the Youth Court and, where allocated, the Crown Court — with the specific procedures and welfare considerations the youth jurisdiction requires.

contactPoint.contactType: Youth defence and police station support

mainEntity.name: My child has been arrested — what do I do first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call 07922 247 999. Police station support can be arranged from the same call. The young person is entitled to have a parent or guardian present at interview.

mainEntity.name: Will my child's case stay in the Youth Court?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most youth matters remain in the Youth Court. Some are sent to the Crown Court depending on the allegation and the client's age. The first call covers which is likely.

mainEntity.name: Can a parent instruct on the young person's behalf?

acceptedAnswer.text: A parent or guardian is involved throughout, but the young person remains the client. The first conference is taken with both on the line.
